title: Refactor tenant hot-row smoothing and online index switchover
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: A small fraction of tenants create disproportionate read/write hot rows in several control-plane tables (tenant_events, project_counters). These hot rows cause tail latency spikes and CPU pinning on certain shards. Past tickets have focused on wide normalization and partitioning, but we still see recurring hot-tenant incidents. This ticket implements a low-risk, reversible approach: introduce a lightweight tenant_access_frequency pipeline and a set of runtime hooks to apply "hot-row smoothing" (auto-surface per-tenant partial indexes, shadow tables, and routing hints), then perform an online index switchover to move heavy-read patterns to optimized indexes without long locks. Goals: reduce 95th/99th percentile latency on control-plane reads by >=30% for affected tenants, reduce CPU tail events, and give an operational rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy tenant_access_frequency materialized view and background scorer; pipeline runs every 5m
Auto-create partial indexes for top-1% tenants using CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY with safe name scheme
Introduce per-tenant shadow tables for the top 10 heaviest tenants and keep them writable via trigger-based dual-write during switchover
Validated 95th and 99th percentile read latency reduction >= 30% for at least two production tenants in staging load test
Rollback procedure documented and verified in staging (drop shadow tables and re-point queries via view swap)
No table-level locks > 1s during switchover in production canary run
migration_steps: Add tenant_access_frequency materialized view that aggregates reads/writes per-tenant per-5m (conservative retention 7d)
Deploy background scorer service that promotes tenants to hot-tier if moving average exceeds threshold
On promotion, create partial indexes: name format idx_hot_<table>_<tenantid>_v1 USING CONCURRENTLY
For the top N tenants (configurable), create shadow tables schema: <table>__hot_<tenantid> and dual-write triggers
Backfill shadow tables with a batched COPY (throttled) and validate row counts/checksums
Swap logical access via an updated view: ALTER VIEW controlplane_<table> to point to COALESCE(hot_table, base_table) pattern with fast update using transactionally-created view
Monitor metrics for 1h during canary; if regressions, execute rollback plan
rollback_plan: If we observe correctness or performance regressions during canary: 1) Disable scorer promotions (stop automatic creation) 2) Repoint application view to base table via ALTER VIEW in a small transaction 3) Disable triggers that route writes to shadow tables 4) Keep shadow tables read-only for postmortem, then drop with DROP TABLE CONCURRENTLY after validation. All steps are documented with exact SQL commands in the Confluence runbook linked below.
safety_and_monitoring: Metric dashboards: controlplane.read_p95, read_p99, cpu_steal, pg_locks, index_creation_duration
Alert: read_p99 increase > 15% for 30m during canary -> auto-rollback job
Sampling: enable query-level sampling for hot-tenants (1%) to compare query plans before/after
Audit: write audit events when scorer promotes/demotes tenant (for rollback tracing)
performance_considerations: We will use CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY to avoid exclusive locks. Dual-write trigger introduces write amplification; only enable for a bounded set of tenants (configurable, default top 10). Background scorer will prefer partial indexes over full indexes to limit index size and maintenance cost. We will measure token/batch CPU and I/O during backfill and throttle backfill to avoid saturating replicas.

Discussed approach with infra and infra-db; decided on partial-index+shadow-table path to avoid wide partitioning work right now.

2026-03-11 Luca Fernandez: Implemented initial tenant_access_frequency materialized view and pushed draft PR for scorer. Performance team suggested a 5m window (vs 1m) to reduce noise — updated the design.

2026-03-12 Priya Nair (DBRE): Reviewed migration steps. Flagged that CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY still holds an ACCESS SHARE lock briefly on some versions; we will measure during canary. Added auditing to capture create index durations.

notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: avoid broad schema rewrites and instead target operational mechanisms that can be rolled forward/back quickly. If the approach proves insufficient for long-term scale, we'll propose a follow-up for tenant-level partitioning or per-tenant micro-shards with online rebalancing.
